note: The SessionStart seat context (hooks/session_start.py) used to hand a fresh agent two things: hooks/seat.md and a one-line pytest check. It said nothing about the decision store built across the brain work (#73-#79), so a cold agent booted blind to what had already been decided and re-proposed closed doors -- the rediscovery tax this store exists to stop paying. This change stands the committed store up every session: it is opened read-only, self-tested with one live verbatim retrieval, and handed to the agent with the exact `nestor --db ... decision check` command, the matcher/bar it keys on, and the exact-wording blind spot stated plainly. The readiness checks were hardened at the same time (no-venv reads as a next step, not an exception) and every section is guarded so a failure is a status line, never a traceback that takes the boot down.

decisions.question: The pre-session hook can surface the decision store, run a boot self-test, or just harden the environment check. Which does it do?
decisions.commitment: All three, composed as guarded sections. build_context() joins seat.md, a hardened pytest-readiness line, and a brain section that opens docs/dogfood/nestor.db read-only, runs one live verbatim retrieval as a self-test, reports the matcher (StringMatcher) and the seal/context bars, states the exact-wording blind spot, and prints the consult command `nestor --db docs/dogfood/nestor.db decision check "<q>"`. Each section runs under _guard(), which turns any exception into one `[check] <label>: unavailable (...)` line so a broken section degrades rather than replacing the whole boot with a traceback.
decisions.why: The user asked to harden what was there and add both the closed-doors digest and the boot self-test, plus stand up a Nestor the session actually uses. One composed context delivers all of it without a second hook, and the fail-open guard is the same posture hooks/before_write already keeps: the seat context is the first thing an agent reads, so a helper that raises would show as a broken boot. A boot section is optional context; a crash in it must not be a boot precondition.

decisions.question: Standing up the brain at boot -- does the hook build or mutate the store when it is missing?
decisions.commitment: No. The hook opens the committed store read-only and closes it; it never rebuilds, seals, or writes. A missing docs/dogfood/nestor.db is reported with the one command that fixes it (`python scripts/dogfood_store.py --rebuild`), not silently rebuilt. The self-test query is pulled from the store's own rows via export_bundle, so nothing is hardcoded to drift out from under it.
decisions.why: A SessionStart hook that mutates the tree is the failure it would be diagnosing -- a boot that changes the repo before the agent has proposed anything inverts propose-before-acting. Reporting the missing store fails loud without acting, and reading the probe question from the store keeps 'the brain answers' a measurement taken at boot rather than an assertion about a fixed string.
